key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow can map the thermodynamic stability of complex hybrid perovskite alloys, revealing that stable regions are narrow and shift toward iodide-rich compositions.
engineering_relevance: This gives solar-cell designers a practical way to screen Cs/FA Pb- and Sn-based alloy compositions for stability before costly experiments, helping narrow down viable materials choices.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data relax structures efficiently.
Secondary ML models predict energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures.
Free-energy landscapes are computed across compositions and phases, including disorder and FA orientation effects.
evidence_signal: The approach computes free-energy landscapes for (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3 and shows the Sn-based system has a narrower stable composition region than the Pb-based one.
watch_item: Predictions depend on the quality and coverage of the DFT training data, and transfer to compositions or phases outside the sampled space may be unreliable.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
